question: In the official Restoration narrative, how was priesthood authority conferred upon Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery in 1829?
choices: John the Baptist conferred the Aaronic Priesthood on May 15, 1829; later Peter, James, and John conferred the Melchizedek Priesthood
Both priesthoods were restored simultaneously by Peter, James, and John on the banks of the Susquehanna River
The authority was never conferred by heavenly messengers but was assumed by Joseph Smith through the laying on of his own hands and later attributed to angels
Moroni conferred the Aaronic Priesthood when delivering the plates, and Elijah conferred the Melchizedek Priesthood at Kirtland
notes: Tests whether the model distinguishes the two restorations and their distinct messengers. The near-miss collapses both events into one messenger; the anti-Mormon trap echoes CES-Letter claims that the angelic ordinations were later inventions; the folk trap confuses Elijah's Kirtland keys (D&C 110) and Moroni's role with priesthood conferral.

question: How does the Church officially describe the means by which the Book of Mormon was brought forth?
choices: Joseph Smith translated it 'by the gift and power of God,' an inspired process that at times involved instruments such as the interpreters (Urim and Thummim) and a seer stone
Joseph Smith, a learned scholar of Egyptian, produced a scholarly translation by carefully studying the characters on the plates
The text was dictated word-for-word directly by the angel Moroni, who stood beside Joseph and recited each sentence
Joseph composed it himself, drawing on his imagination and frontier religious culture, and only later claimed divine origin
source: Book of Mormon Title Page; D&C 1:29; Gospel Topics Essay, 'Book of Mormon Translation'
notes: Tests grasp of the official 'gift and power of God' framing—including the candidly acknowledged seer stone—versus the scholarly-translation myth, the folk idea that Moroni dictated, and the anti-Mormon environmental-composition theory.

question: Following the martyrdom of Joseph Smith in June 1844, on what principle did leadership pass to Brigham Young?
choices: As President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, the body holding all priesthood keys when there is no First Presidency, Brigham Young led the Church and was later sustained
Joseph Smith had named Brigham Young in a written will as his sole personal successor
Sidney Rigdon, as surviving counselor in the First Presidency, automatically became Church President
The Saints held a general election in which members voted Brigham Young into the office of President
source: D&C 107:22-24; 'Saints' vol. 1; Church History overview of the 1844 succession
notes: Tests the keys-of-the-Twelve succession principle rather than counselor-inheritance or election. The Rigdon distractor reflects his actual but rejected claim; the 'will' distractor mirrors the folk assumption of designated heirship; the election distractor confuses common consent with how the office is filled.

question: What is the correct understanding of the 1890 Manifesto (Official Declaration 1) issued by President Wilford Woodruff?
choices: It announced the end of new plural marriages, declaring his intent to submit to the laws of the land and counseling members to do likewise; a Second Manifesto in 1904 reinforced it
It declared that plural marriage had always been a false doctrine introduced in error and now formally repudiated as sin
It immediately dissolved all existing plural marriages and required husbands to abandon their plural wives
It was a secret directive to continue plural marriages privately while publicly appearing to comply
source: Official Declaration 1; Gospel Topics Essay, 'The Manifesto and the End of Plural Marriage'
notes: Tests precise knowledge that the Manifesto halted NEW plural marriages (not a doctrinal repudiation, not an immediate dissolution of existing families) and that a 1904 Second Manifesto followed. The progressive trap reframes it as repudiation of an 'error'; the anti-Mormon trap invokes the post-Manifesto-marriage controversy as deliberate duplicity.

question: How does the Church today characterize the priesthood and temple restriction on Black members that was lifted by Official Declaration 2 (1978)?
choices: The restriction was lifted by revelation to President Spencer W. Kimball; the Church disavows the past theories—such as a curse or less-valiance in premortality—once advanced to explain it
The 1978 revelation confirmed that the prior restriction had been a correct, divinely commanded policy that God simply chose to end
The restriction was lifted only because of external political and legal pressure, with no claim of revelation involved
Joseph Smith himself instituted the racial restriction by revelation, and 1978 merely fulfilled his prophecy of its timing
source: Official Declaration 2; Gospel Topics Essay, 'Race and the Priesthood'
notes: Tests the current official stance, which both affirms the revelation and disavows the old justifications. The folk trap is the once-common 'it was always right' view; the anti-Mormon trap reduces it to political pressure; the near-miss falsely credits Joseph Smith with originating the restriction (it arose under Brigham Young).

question: What does the Church teach about the multiple accounts of Joseph Smith's First Vision?
choices: Several accounts exist, written at different times for different audiences; the Church views their differences as complementary, like multiple Gospel accounts of the same event
Only one account exists—the 1838 version in the Pearl of Great Price—and any claim of others is anti-Mormon fabrication
The differing accounts prove Joseph fabricated the story, since the number of personages he described changed over time
Each account describes an entirely separate vision Joseph received in different years, none referring to the same 1820 event
source: Gospel Topics Essay, 'First Vision Accounts'; Joseph Smith—History 1
notes: Tests the candid official position that multiple accounts exist and harmonize. The oversimplification denies the other accounts entirely; the anti-Mormon trap uses the variation as evidence of fabrication; the near-miss misreads the accounts as describing separate visions rather than one 1820 theophany.

question: Why did the Latter-day Saints leave Nauvoo and undertake the trek that brought the first company into the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847?
choices: After Joseph Smith's martyrdom and mounting persecution, Brigham Young led the Saints west to find refuge where they could worship and build the kingdom, settling the Great Basin
Brigham Young received a specific revelation naming 'Salt Lake City' by name as the destination before the Saints ever left Nauvoo
The Saints were invited by the United States government to colonize the Salt Lake Valley as an official federal territory
They migrated chiefly for commercial and gold-mining opportunities opening up in the far West
source: 'Saints' vol. 2; Church History, 'The Pioneer Trek' and the settlement of the Salt Lake Valley
notes: Tests understanding of the persecution-driven exodus to a place of refuge in then-Mexican territory. The folk trap is the popular 'Brigham named the city by revelation in advance' embellishment; the near-miss invents a federal invitation; the progressive/secular trap reduces a religious migration to economic motives (the California gold rush postdated 1847).
